visualReview.notes: Principal palace exterior across the White Horse courtyard ranges/northern range, main front pavilion/two mapped curved horseshoe stair flights, Gallery of Francis I/Cour de la Fontaine, eastern oval court/chapel and northeast ranges. Open courts, pale masonry, crossed casements, steep slate roofscape/dormers and tall brick chimneys. Actual1.5m arched lower gate recess/soffit/threshold, separate4.9m upper landing/door and stepped flights with closed railings; nine2.7m recessed gallery arch bays with opaque back glazing as an exterior proxy. Hidden geometry/ornament reconstructed. Fixed the dark wall texture and unsupported pavilion projection in the same author/inspect pass.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Five existing256px graphs shared by six textured roles/draws: stone_limestone_raw pale walls/trim, slate roof, brick_flemish stacks, storefront opaque crossed glazing and metal_painted static doors/dark trim. Generic limestone substitutes for exact historic masonry/weathering; plain pediments/fields omit sculpture/inscriptions. No new graph/private atlas/embedded images. One skyline draw, linear palette tints, separate POSITION/NORMAL streams and equal CPU-GPU accounting. Every native textured run reads each required graph once; all LOD unloads release model geometry.

fidelityReview.notes: Photo-led exterior reconstruction from two ordinary pictures and mapped footprints. Most heights are absent; use8..20m working eaves, main front12.5m/central pavilion19m, gallery13.5m, south range11.5m, eastern chapel20m and northern range11.5m. Two northeast part tags5/8m are unqualified; exact eaves/ridges are not surveyed. Medial-ridge hip roofs reconstruct the complex unseen roof junctions; dome-like turrets are omitted where unsupported. Repeated windows/quoins/dormers/chimneys and plain pediments abstract the Renaissance detail. Horseshoe stair flights rise4.9m above the working floor; central lower arched gate1.5m recess and upper landing/door are distinct. Gallery has actual recessed arch bays. No copied ornament/artwork. Five existing256px graphs shared by six roles: stone_limestone_raw for pale walls/trim, slate, brick_flemish, storefront and metal_painted. Skyline preserves court holes and simplifies the lower range heights/footprints within5m; district rounds eaves and flattens portals; street has coarser roof ridges and fewer windows/dormers. The closeup preserves full mapped exterior topology. Ornament, sculpture, art and lettering are abstracted or omitted. The broad exterior is a medium-fi reconstruction. Most heights/eave/ridge levels, exact facade/bay/dormer/stack counts and unseen elevations/roof junctions are approximate. The northern relation and all19 map records are included; independent peripheral stable/administration buildings and garden/fountain context remain procedural. No furnished rooms, copied arms/inscriptions/sculpture/art, flags or walk-through gallery interior. Exact court grades/thresholds/accessibility and physical phone/laptop/dense-city timings remain unverified.

frameReview.method: Actually inspected48 current frames in six labeled contact sheets plus final native White Horse facade, gallery court and horseshoe entrance at full resolution. Two ordinary pictures and standard PMTiles/Mapzen guided one author/inspect/fix pass. Changed dark weathered limestone to the shared pale raw-limestone graph; cropped the raised central pavilion to its supported mapped footprint; aligned recesses with actual mapped wall edges, closed railing ends and refined street arch curvature. Medial roof samples preserve steep continuous ridges; adjacent vertical bands merge without changing their exterior envelope.

limitations: Principal exterior of the Palace of Fontainebleau, including the mapped White Horse courtyard ranges/north range, central pavilion and two curved horseshoe stair flights, Gallery of Francis I/Cour de la Fontaine ranges, eastern oval court/chapel and northeast service court ranges. Pale masonry, crossed casements, steep slate roofs/dormers and brick chimneys. Open courtyards and independent buildings remain. No furnished rooms, copied crests/inscriptions/sculpture, flags, gardens, fountain sculpture or peripheral stable/administration buildings.
